title: Latinx Workers
text:
NSF-funded collaborative research project: Should I Stay or Should I Go? Understanding the Retention of Latinx in Engineering Jobs. Designed and applied quantitative methods (survey design, multilevel modeling) to understand factors driving career persistence and attrition among Latinx engineers.
Award: NSF 2000607, $1,546,428 (2020–2025). PIs: Lisa Y. Flores (University of Missouri), Rachel L. Navarro (University of North Dakota). Role: Key Personnel.

title: Flipped Mathematics Study
text:
NSF-funded research investigating how flipped-classroom instruction affects students’ learning of mathematics across diverse classroom settings.
Award: NSF DRL-1721025, $539,011 (2017–2021). PIs: Zandra de Araujo, Samuel J. Otten, Ze Wang, James Tarr.

title: Books
text:
Quantitative Foundations in Educational Research
A self-contained introduction to applied statistics for educational and social-science research: descriptive statistics, probability, sampling, inference, regression, and ANOVA. Developed for ESC_PS 8850, the master’s-level methods course I taught at the University of Missouri. Lecture slides → · Previous site →

title: Books
section: Structural Equation Modeling Using R and Mplus
text:
Structural Equation Modeling Using R and Mplus
A practical introduction to structural equation modeling with worked examples in both R (lavaan) and Mplus. Covers measurement models, path analysis, latent variable models, model fit, and multi-group / multilevel extensions. Built around ESC_PS 9710, a doctoral course I taught at the University of Missouri. Lecture slides → · Previous site →

title: Ze Wang
text:
I am a Research Scientist at Amazon Web Services, based in Ashburn, VA. I lead end-to-end analytical and machine learning initiatives that shape product decisions, automate data pipelines, and improve operational efficiency, and I serve as the certification psychometrician for multiple AWS certification exams. My work bridges deep statistical expertise — causal inference, structural equation modeling, Bayesian methods, item response theory — with scalable Python, R, SQL, and AWS infrastructure.
Before AWS, I was a tenured Associate Professor of Statistics, Measurement, and Evaluation in Education at the University of Missouri (2008–2022). My academic research focused on statistical modeling using large-scale assessment data, measurement, scale development, and program evaluation. I co-developed the Classroom Engagement Inventory and authored 50+ peer-reviewed papers, three books, and six book chapters.

title: Ze Wang
text:
What I work on

Causal inference and experimental design. Designing observational and quasi-experimental studies for product and operational decisions.
Psychometrics and measurement. Item response theory, structural equation modeling, scale development, standard setting.
Machine learning at AWS scale. Predictive modeling of operational metrics; balancing performance with interpretability for business stakeholders.
Generative AI applications. Internal AWS GenAI projects; review of GenAI research proposals.
